column1: # The library's NACA sections with their trailing edges bent down as brakes bend them, solved with mfoil
# Source: computed by this tool — src/core/mfoil.js (the port of K. J. Fidkowski's mfoil, held to
#   mfoil.py to 3e-13 in data/reference/mfoil-sections.tsv) on the sections brakesection.js bends
#   (brakeBentPoints: the chord behind 65% bent into a circular arc, its length kept, the surfaces
#   carried on it), swept by brakeSectionSteps from the angle that converges first, each solve from
#   its neighbour's boundary layer, a failure tried again from half way and then cold
# measure: computed, by mfoil.js; converged solutions only (a missing angle did not converge)
# section   the NACA four-digit code, nacaSection(code) as the tool builds it (80 points)
# bend_deg  the trailing edge's slope at the end of the arc, degrees; its drop is
#           0.35 (1 - cos bend) / bend of the chord: 0.061 at 20 degrees, 0.117 at 40
# alpha_deg the angle of attack against the unbent chord, degrees
# cl cd cdf cm  lift, drag, its skin-friction part, and the moment about the quarter chord
# xtr_upper xtr_lower  transition as x/c; 0 where the boundary layer stays laminar to the end
# Re 1.4 million is the default wing's at trim on its mean chord; the tool uses these where the
# design's section is one of these as built and its Reynolds number is within half again of it,
# and solves its own otherwise (brakeSectionSteps, about two minutes).
